title: Anthropic IPO launch shifts toward mid-October
content:
Anthropic is expected to begin marketing its initial public offering in mid-October at the earliest and complete the listing days before the U.S. midterm elections in November, people familiar with the matter said on Friday.
The artificial intelligence company had been expected to make its IPO prospectus public as early as next week, two of the people said, a crucial step that would kick off the final stages of the offering. Now that is not expected until late September, the people added, cautioning that the plans, including the timing, are subject to change.
The shift pushes back what some investors have said could be a $2 trillion listing, one of the largest IPOs ever attempted and a major test of public-market appetite for the rapidly growing artificial intelligence industry.
Companies frequently adjust their IPO schedules as they work through market conditions, regulatory reviews and other preparations, so such changes are not unusual.
As part of the IPO process, Anthropic is looking to finalize a $15 billion revolving credit facility, after which analysts, including those at banks involved in the financing, are expected to meet with the company, one person said. Bloomberg News earlier reported that Anthropic was in talks to expand the facility to $15 billion.
Companies typically leave a few weeks between analyst meetings and making the IPO prospectus public, although Anthropic is expected to have a tighter window because analysts already know the company well, the person said.
Anthropic declined to comment.
The offering is expected to be one of the most closely anticipated IPOs ever, as investors look to public markets for exposure to the rapidly growing artificial intelligence industry. It could come alongside potential listings from other AI companies, including OpenAI. Elon Musk's SpaceX went public in June at a record $1.77 trillion valuation.
Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Citi are among the banks working with Anthropic on the IPO, according to people familiar with the matter.
The banks declined to comment.

report.summary: Anthropic's IPO slides: prospectus late September, marketing mid-October, aiming for listing before U.S. midterms in a possible $2 trillion debut.
report.background: Anthropic, the AI safety-focused company behind Claude, was expected to publish its IPO prospectus as early as next week, but sources say this has slipped to late September. Marketing the offering will not begin until mid-October at the earliest, with the listing expected to complete before the U.S. midterm elections in November. Companies frequently adjust IPO timelines because of market conditions, regulatory reviews, and preparation work. The listing is seen as one of the largest ever attempted, with investor speculation pointing to a roughly $2 trillion valuation. This would serve as a major public-market test for the AI industry, especially as OpenAI and other AI firms also weigh listings. SpaceX's June IPO at a $1.77 trillion valuation raised the bar, but Anthropic's deal would still be a defining event for AI investing.
key_points: Anthropic planned to publish its IPO prospectus as early as next week, but now expects late September. Marketing the offering will start mid-October at the earliest, and the listing is expected to be completed before the U.S. midterm elections in November. Sources caution plans may change.

Investors describe a possible $2 trillion valuation, making it one of the largest IPOs ever attempted. This creates a major test for public-market appetite for AI, and could set precedent for other high-profile AI listings such as OpenAI and comparable mega-cap tech offerings.

Anthropic is working to finalize a $15 billion revolving credit facility as part of IPO preparations. Afterward, bank analysts will meet with the company, and executives expect a tight window to go public since analysts already know Anthropic well, allowing faster progression from meetings to prospectus.

Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Citi are among the banks managing the IPO, according to people familiar with the matter. The banks declined to comment, and Anthropic also declined to comment. Delays in IPO scheduling are common due to market conditions and regulatory review.
report.impact: Anthropic's IPO timing shift suggests even the most prominent AI companies must manage regulatory and market cycles carefully. A successful listing would give Anthropic public capital to fund large-scale model training and infrastructure, potentially accelerating product competition with OpenAI and others. Developers may benefit from more stable APIs and resources, while public investors will demand clearer revenue and cost paths, introducing stricter scrutiny of safety-first positioning. For regular users, a large IPO could eventually lead to broader consumer AI integration, but also raises questions about accountability, pricing, and whether AI growth can justify such high valuations. This is a moment that will test how the entire AI sector is valued.

For valuation and peer-company context, monitor financial data with `yfinance` or open-source datasets like `stock-market-dataset`. Bloomberg Terminal and PitchBook also offer due diligence tools.
